solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: AC/DC featured in newspaper piece by E Bloom

indicators.note: something featured in a publication appears inside it, so one part is set within the other

parts.note: a regular article in a newspaper
AC/DC is slang for bisexual, shortened to BI
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rock band gets a write-up in the paper alongside a piece by a contributor called E Bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: AC/DC looks like the rock band, but it is old slang for bisexual. 'Bloom' at the end reads as a surname; it is the definition, a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: The columbine is a garden flower, the aquilegia, so it is one example of a bloom.

clue.text: Jest involving me now crushed in disappointment

indicators.note: to involve is to take in or include, so one piece wraps around another
something crushed is mangled out of shape, so the letters lose their order

parts.note: to cod is to joke or hoax someone
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone whose joke has fallen flat feels crushed and disappointed.
explanation.walkthrough: COD (to jest) wraps around ME NOW, and then the whole lot is jumbled; 'crushed' applies to all eight letters, not just to ME NOW.
explanation.definitionFit: A comedown is a letdown, a fall from expectation or status, so it is a synonym for disappointment.

clue.text: Joins course for coastal drivers?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: connects, as a verb
second meaning: a seaside golf course, where drivers are golf clubs

explanation.surface: Someone takes up a route meant for motorists along the coast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drivers' suggests motorists, but they are golf clubs; a links is a golf course on sandy ground by the sea, and the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a verb for connecting things and also a noun for seaside golf courses such as St Andrews.

clue.text: Soldier serving at sea must consume fish spread

indicators.note: to consume is to swallow, so one piece is taken inside another

parts.note: a marine is a soldier who serves aboard ship
the gar is a long-snouted fish

explanation.surface: A sailor-soldier has to eat a fish spread on board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fish spread' wants to be a single food; 'fish' is the wordplay and 'spread' is the definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Margarine is a butter substitute that people put on bread, so it is a kind of spread.

clue.text: Temporary home — call to accommodate one

parts.note: at home means in

indicators.note: to accommodate a guest is to put them up inside, so one piece holds another

parts.note: to term something is to call or name it
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A makeshift dwelling is offered to take in a single lodger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Temporary home' reads as one phrase; 'Temporary' alone is the definition and 'home' gives IN.
explanation.definitionFit: An interim arrangement is provisional, lasting only until something permanent replaces it, so the adjective matches temporary.

clue.text: Artist, composer and author lacking answer

indicators.note: lacking something means being without it, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: Edward Elgar, the English composer
Umberto Eco, the Italian novelist
A is the standard abbreviation for answer

explanation.surface: A list of three creative people, the last of whom has no reply to give.
explanation.walkthrough: ELGAR plus ECO, then the A of answer is taken out of the combination.
explanation.definitionFit: El Greco was a Cretan-born painter working in Renaissance Spain, so he is an example of an artist.

clue.text: Loiner's locale has the advantage we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is a spoken version, so the sound matters rather than the spelling

parts.note: someone who is ahead in a contest leads

explanation.surface: A local's home town is said to be ahead of its rivals.
explanation.walkthrough: A Loiner is the old nickname for a person from Leeds, a city in Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Natives of the city are called Loiners, so their home place is this Yorkshire city by local demonym.

clue.text: Sacred flower for all to see in quite a bunch

indicators.note: one thing being in another puts it inside

parts.note: lots means a good many
U is the British film certificate meaning suitable for everyone

explanation.surface: A holy bloom is displayed openly among a large bouquet.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the British cinema rating for films anyone may watch, the equivalent of the American G.
explanation.definitionFit: The lotus is a water plant held holy in Hinduism and Buddhism, so it is a sacred flower.

clue.text: Disease rampant on the way in alien world

indicators.note: one thing being in another puts it inside

parts.note: ET is the film alien

indicators.note: in a down clue, one thing on another sits above it, so the pieces stack in order
rampant means running wild, so the letters run out of control

parts.note: pox is a disease
a lane is a way or road

explanation.surface: An epidemic spreads along the road into a strange planet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alien world' reads as the definition, but 'alien' is ET, wrapped around the rest; only 'world' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: An exoplanet is a planet orbiting a star other than our sun, so it is another world.

clue.text: Warm reddish-brown colour new in Italian walled city

indicators.note: one thing being in another puts it inside

parts.note: Siena is a walled city in Tuscany
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A fresh shade appears in a Tuscan town.
explanation.walkthrough: The pigment is named after the city itself, which is spelt with one N.
explanation.definitionFit: Sienna is an earth pigment; burnt sienna gives the warm reddish-brown tone used by painters.

clue.text: Cassandra's edging away from Balearic island ward?

indicators.note: going away from somewhere means leaving it, so letters are removed

parts.note: one of the Balearic Islands in the Mediterranean

indicators.note: an edging is the border of something, so only the outer letters are wanted

parts.note: the first and last letters of the name

explanation.surface: Cassandra is leaving a Mediterranean island hospital ward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ward' looks like part of a hospital; with the question mark it means a person under a guardian's care, typically a child.
explanation.definitionFit: A ward of court is usually a child under legal protection, so a minor is an example of one.

clue.text: Pie-eyed guy's precarious course

parts.note: both are slang for drunk
a guy is a rope steadying a tent, and the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A drunk man is weaving an unsteady path home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guy' is not a man but a guy rope; the 's is read as 'is', joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Walking a tightrope means following a narrow, risky line, a figurative image for any dangerous path.

clue.text: In love's absence does couple hit rock bottom?

indicators.note: in the absence of something means without it, so a letter goes missing

parts.note: taken as written
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
a couple is a pair

explanation.surface: A couple whose love has gone wonder whether they have reached their lowest point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In ... absence' means without, so O leaves DOES. 'Despair' is a verb here, matching 'hit rock bottom'.
explanation.definitionFit: To despair is to lose all hope, and reaching rock bottom is the emotional low where that happens.

clue.text: Refusal to welcome Liberal is recalled in letter

indicators.note: to recall is to call back, so the letters run backwards
to welcome a guest is to let them in, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a casual no
L is the abbreviation for Liberal
taken as written

explanation.surface: A party refuses entry to a Liberal, which is reported in a letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letter' looks like correspondence; it is a letter of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Epsilon is the fifth character of the Greek alphabet, so it is one letter.

clue.text: Writer's pleasure: this writer's off to tour Lake District initially

indicators.note: to tour a place is to go round it, so one piece surrounds another

parts.note: will means wish or pleasure, as in 'at your will'
the setter's 'this writer' is I, and 's stands for am
to be off is to be going

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only first letters are taken

parts.note: first letters of the two words

explanation.surface: An author says he is delighted to be setting out on a trip round the Lakes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This writer' is the setter's way of saying I or ME; here 'this writer's' becomes I AM. The Lake District is a hilly region of north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: William Golding wrote Lord of the Flies and won the Nobel Prize, so he is a writer.

clue.text: Abhorrent to Holmes, criminally hiding ace

indicators.note: to hide something is to keep it within, so one piece is tucked inside
criminally suggests something crooked, so the letters are twisted out of order

parts.note: taken as written
A is the abbreviation for ace in cards

explanation.surface: Sherlock Holmes finds a crook who is concealing a top card hateful.
explanation.walkthrough: Holmes is not a detective clue here; his name and 'to' simply supply letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something loathsome causes disgust and hatred, so the adjective is a straightforward synonym for abhorrent.

clue.text: Velocity's elevated rate in starless region

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising something makes it read upwards, so its letters run backwards

parts.note: velocity is speed, and the 's stands for is
pace is rate of movement

explanation.surface: A physics note says velocity means a high rate across the empty void.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'Velocity's' is read as 'is', so speed is what is elevated; 'rate' simply follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep space is the vast emptiness between stars and galaxies, far from any star, hence a starless region.

clue.text: Given similar roles, produce manuscript when entering court

parts.note: to type is to produce a typescript

indicators.note: to enter a place is to go inside it, so one piece is placed within another

parts.note: CT is the abbreviation for court
as means when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: An actor drafts a script while going into court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' is not a legal venue to the solver but just the abbreviation CT, which is opened up to admit AS.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor who is typecast is repeatedly given the same kind of part, a verb in the past participle.

clue.text: Keeping a pretty busy axe shaped the battle record

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it within, so one piece is enclosed
shaping something remakes its form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A warrior keeps a much-used axe in shape, mirroring the account of a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: The Bayeux Tapestry is the embroidered strip recording the Norman Conquest of England in 1066.
explanation.definitionFit: This embroidered cloth depicts the Battle of Hastings in pictures, so it serves as the record of that battle.

clue.text: Ten work with nurse filling hopper

indicators.note: a filling sits inside something, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: the Roman numeral for ten
EN is an enrolled nurse
a work, especially of music

explanation.surface: Ten staff and a nurse are loading a hopper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hopper' looks like a funnel-shaped container, but it is something that hops. EN is an enrolled nurse, a British nursing grade.
explanation.definitionFit: Xenopus is the genus of African clawed frogs, and a frog is an animal that jumps.

clue.text: Plain person, perhaps Scarlett carries old man around

indicators.note: turning around faces the other way, so the letters run backwards
carrying something means holding it, so one piece is held inside another

parts.note: Scarlett O'Hara, heroine of Gone with the Wind
pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: An unglamorous woman, maybe Scarlett, is carrying her elderly father about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plain person' sounds like someone unattractive; it means a person of the Great Plains. 'Perhaps' marks Scarlett as one example of an O'Hara.
explanation.definitionFit: The Arapaho are a Native American people of the Great Plains, so one is a Plains person.

clue.text: Kind of chop academician fed to a shrew?

indicators.note: food fed to someone goes inside them, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: Kate is the shrew in Shakespeare's The Taming of the Shrew
RA is a Royal Academician

explanation.surface: A shrew is offered a chop from a scholar, as if it were a pet's dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chop' looks like a cut of meat to feed the animal; it is a hand strike. The shrew is not the mammal but Shakespeare's heroine.
explanation.definitionFit: A karate chop is a sharp edge-of-hand blow from the Japanese martial art, so the word names that kind of chop.

clue.text: Long article about Astyanax's origin, Greek in Homer

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round another

parts.note: to ache for something is to long for it

indicators.note: an origin is a starting point, so only the first letter is wanted

parts.note: first letter of the name
the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A lengthy piece of writing about the origins of Astyanax, the son of Hector in Homer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long article' reads as a lengthy essay, but 'Long' is a verb meaning yearn, and the article is a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer calls the Greeks besieging Troy the Achaeans, so an Achaean is a Greek in his epics.

clue.text: Almost beheaded — before dawn?

indicators.note: beheading takes off the top, so the first letter is lost

parts.note: nearly means almost

explanation.surface: Someone was very nearly executed in the hours before daybreak.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that 'before dawn' is only one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Anything happening before dawn happens at an early hour, so the adjective fits as an example.

clue.text: Many a witch's death here in question

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the place of execution, read literally, where witches were burned
second meaning: being risked or under consideration

explanation.surface: Where a witch died is the matter under debate.
explanation.walkthrough: The first meaning is literal: accused witches were burnt tied to a post, the stake. The second is the idiom for what is being risked.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for something being risked or under discussion, and literally describes being tied to a burning post.

clue.text: Measure of acidity in beer for Phoenician character?

parts.note: ale is a type of beer
pH is the scale measuring acidity

explanation.surface: Someone checks the acidity in their beer, wondering about a Phoenician figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Character' suggests a person; it is a written letter. The question mark covers the Phoenician origin: aleph is the first letter of the Phoenician and Hebrew alphabets.
explanation.definitionFit: Aleph began the Phoenician alphabet and is still the first Hebrew letter, so it is a Phoenician character.

clue.text: Different approach needed for penning year books

indicators.note: to pen an animal is to shut it in, so one piece encloses another
something different has been altered, so the letters change their order

parts.note: taken as written
Y is the abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: A new method is required for writing an annual series of volumes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Year books' reads as annuals; 'books' alone is the definition, and Y from 'year' is penned into the mixed letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Apocrypha are the biblical books outside the accepted canon, so the word names a set of books.

clue.text: Knight occupying space in which scutarius fought

definitions.note: a descriptive clause standing for the place

indicators.note: to occupy a place is to be inside it, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: an area is a space
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A knight takes the ground where a Roman shield-bearer once battled.
explanation.walkthrough: A scutarius was a gladiator armed with a large shield, the scutum. 'Space' belongs to the wordplay, not the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Roman gladiators fought in the sanded arena of an amphitheatre, so that is where a scutarius did battle.

clue.text: For one buried in fenland see mournful poem

indicators.note: something buried in the ground lies inside it, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city and diocese in the Fens of East Anglia
e.g. means for example, for one

explanation.surface: Someone buried in the flat marshland is mourned in verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' looks like a verb of looking; it is a bishop's diocese, and the Fens are low marshy farmland in eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: An elegy is a poem of lament, usually for the dead, so it is a mournful poem.

clue.text: Good person with talk on a certain singer

indicators.note: in an across clue, one thing on another follows it, so the pieces line up in that order

parts.note: ST is a saint, a good person
'a certain' person is 'one' person
chat is talk

explanation.surface: A kind person gives a talk about a particular vocalist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Singer' suggests a performer; it is a songbird.
explanation.definitionFit: The stonechat is a small European songbird named for its call like pebbles clicking, so it is a singer.
